items.title: requests 2.32.0+ does not work with truststore library
items.body:
## Problem
Starting with the release 2.32.0 of the requests library the truststore library always leads to an recursion error. I was able to reproduce this on different Windows, Linux (Ubuntu) and macOS machines.

The crulpit seems to be the added "preloaded ssl context", which does not work well with truststore injection. While it seems to use urllib3 under the hood, the patched SSLContext is not really used.

## Fix
Proposed fix is to import the `requests.adapter` package and patch the context accordingly with a truststore patched SSLContext, finished up in https://github.com/sethmlarson/truststore/pull/164

## Related
- https://github.com/sethmlarson/truststore/issues/155
- https://github.com/sethmlarson/truststore/issues/121

items.title: `SSLContext` recursion error strikes again (potential bug as well)
items.body:
Related to this older [Issue](https://github.com/sethmlarson/truststore/issues/121), we started to encounter this problem through our [**robocorp**](https://github.com/robocorp/robocorp) libraries (where injection gets [done](https://github.com/robocorp/robocorp/blob/master/tasks/src/robocorp/tasks/cli.py#L28-L65) -- so at CLI level, not library) and now I observe it even in our CI during the [test runs](https://github.com/robocorp/truststore/actions/runs/9777809056/job/26993266676?pr=2). (while I couldn't reproduce locally on the same system and Python version)

1. Question is, did something change in the _ssl.py_ so that this started to appear with the later Py3.10.x versions?
2. And why is the super class invoked like this: `_original_super_SSLContext = super(_original_SSLContext, _original_SSLContext)`? Even in the standard `ssl` module I see the same pattern when calling the `verify_mode` method. By looking at the docs we have the following:
   > super(type, type2) -> bound super object; requires issubclass(type2, type)
   ```python
   @verify_mode.setter
   def verify_mode(self, value):
       super(SSLContext, SSLContext).verify_mode.__set__(self, value)
   ```
   L.E.: That's all good, as expected. (as we get the super class of the first argument while passing the second for change)
3. Don't we have a bug here with this code (__api.py_)?
   ```python
   @verify_flags.setter
   def verify_flags(self, value: ssl.VerifyFlags) -> None:
       _original_super_SSLContext.verify_flags.__set__(  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
           self._ctx, value
       )
   ```
   as clearly we [don't have](https://github.com/robocorp/truststore/actions/runs/9774743548/job/26983664502?pr=1) `.verify_flags` available with PyPI.
